name: Why is dirty water coming up through my drain?

mainEntity.name: Why is dirty water coming up through my drain?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dirty water backing up through a drain typically indicates a blockage or issue within your plumbing system, often in the main sewer line. Common causes include tree roots invading pipes, accumulation of grease, hair, and debris, or a collapsed pipe section. When the wastewater can't flow freely through the main line, it seeks the path of least resistance, which is often the lowest drain in your home, like a shower, tub, or toilet. Identifying the exact cause requires a professional assessment, often with camera inspection.
acceptedAnswer.description: Dirty water coming up through a drain usually signals a blockage in your main sewer line from tree roots, grease, or debris. A professional inspection is needed to pinpoint the cause.
